title: Texture Filtering
summary: Official Derivative texturing page for texture filtering, covering nearest, linear, and mipmap linear filtering, TOP Common page smoothness controls, MAT texture-sampling filter type, mipmap fallbacks, and anisotropic filtering.
guidance: Use this article when a plan needs to trade pixel-perfect sampling against smoother scaling in TOP viewers, MAT textures, or GLSL sampling.
Nearest filtering samples one closest pixel and is useful for pixel-perfect results.
Linear filtering blends nearby pixels, while Mipmap Linear blends between mipmap levels as well.
Input Smoothness affects how a TOP operation samples its input TOPs.
Viewer Smoothness only changes how the TOP viewer and network background display the texture; it does not change node texture data or MAT sampling.
For MAT texture parameters, open the + button controls and set Filter Type to Nearest, Linear, or Mipmap Linear.
Use Anisotropic Filtering when textured geometry quality depends on the angle of polygons relative to the camera.
